name: Keywords Everywhere
tagline: Browser extension that overlays search volume, CPC and competition data on Google and a dozen other sites.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The extension itself is trivial: inject a sidebar into the Google results page, render some numbers, done. An agent will have that working before your coffee cools. The problem is where the numbers come from: monthly search volume, CPC and competition are licensed and modelled data, and the whole product is a thin skin over that pipe. You can replicate the skin and then you need an upstream, which means a Google Ads account in good standing with a developer token, or a paid per-request API, either of which costs money and bureaucracy. You end up paying someone for data anyway, just with worse caching and no YouTube, Amazon or Etsy overlays.
coreLoopDIY: A local Chrome extension that injects a keyword panel into Google search results, fed by your own Google Ads Keyword Planner credentials through a small caching proxy on localhost.
requirements: Google Ads account with API access and an approved developer token, or a paid keyword data API key
Node 20+ and a Chromium browser you are willing to load an unpacked extension into
Acceptance that Keyword Planner returns bucketed volume ranges, not precise numbers
whatYouLose: Volume and CPC for non-Google surfaces: YouTube, Amazon, Etsy, Bing, eBay, Pinterest
The blended and smoothed volume estimates, which are closer to reality than raw Keyword Planner buckets
Trend history, related keywords, People Also Search For, and the one-click CSV export
Working on a fresh machine or a phone without redoing the OAuth dance
Someone else absorbing API quota limits, rate limiting and upstream schema changes
moatNotes: The licensing and modelling of search volume is the product. The UI is a content script.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative to a few dollars of credits is a Google Ads developer token application, an OAuth flow, and volume data that arrives as ranges like 1K to 10K instead of a number you can sort a spreadsheet by. People buying this are doing keyword research, not building keyword tooling, and the per-lookup cost is small enough that nobody audits it. The multi-site overlays matter too: once you are used to seeing volume on YouTube and Amazon, a Google-only panel feels broken.
notes: The overlay is an afternoon, the data behind it is not. The moat is licensed clickstream and ad-platform volume data plus the deals to resell it per keyword.
prompt:
Build a local Chrome extension plus proxy called "kw-panel" that overlays keyword metrics on Google search results, using my own Google Ads API credentials.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Chrome MV3 extension, plain TypeScript, no framework, no bundler beyond esbuild.
- Local proxy: Node 20, Express, better-sqlite3 for cache. No Docker.
- Everything runs on my machine. No hosted backend, no accounts, no telemetry.

Proxy (server/):
- POST /metrics takes { keywords: string[], geo: string, lang: string }.
- Calls the Google Ads API KeywordPlanIdeaService.GenerateKeywordIdeas endpoint for historical metrics: avg monthly searches, competition level, low and high top-of-page bid micros.
- Auth via OAuth2 refresh token. Read GOOGLE_ADS_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_ADS_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_ADS_REFRESH_TOKEN, GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN, GOOGLE_ADS_CUSTOMER_ID from .env. Ship .env.example, never commit .env.
- Cache every keyword result in SQLite for 30 days, keyed by keyword + geo + lang. Serve from cache first and only hit the API for misses. Batch misses in groups of 20.
- If credentials are missing, return a clear error the extension can render instead of crashing.

Extension (extension/):
- Content script on google.com/search: read the query from the URL, read the "Related searches" and "People also ask" strings already on the page as the related-keyword list.
- Inject a panel in the right rail: the main query first, then related terms, each row showing volume, competition, and estimated CPC from the bid range.
- Sort by volume descending. Add a "Copy as CSV" button that puts the table on the clipboard.
- Options page for geo and language, stored in chrome.storage.sync.
- Background service worker proxies fetches to http://localhost:8787 so the content script does not trip CORS.

Out of scope, do not build: YouTube, Amazon, Bing or Etsy overlays, trend charts, keyword difficulty scores, a credit system, any login.

Deliver a README that states plainly which Google Ads API prerequisites I must obtain myself, and warns that Keyword Planner returns bucketed volume ranges rather than exact numbers.
